headline: New 3-month buy: General Dynamics at $372.59 on a record $220 billion backlog while AI stocks sulk; no Bold Bet, Max leans the Hornets at 37.5¢ (+1.6 pts); Vikings lean lost 19-15
top_call: Buy General Dynamics for the next 3 months. While the AI trade nurses a brutal October, GD just beat, raised its 2026 outlook and booked a record $220.3 billion backlog, Jefferies lifted its target to $455, and it trades near 20x forward earnings above its 50-day. Graded against the S&P 500, like everything else.
backdrop: Stock futures are bouncing after a dismal October for tech: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.9% early Monday, with oil down more than 4% on U.S.-Iran talk hopes. Apple and Palantir report after the bell, the midterms are Tuesday and the October jobs report lands Friday.

finance.label: GD
finance.entry_note: Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 30 close (Monday edition, before the open)
finance.why: Beat and raise, record $220.3B backlog after 14 new subs, Jefferies to $455; ~20x forward earnings, above its 50-day.
finance.risk: Defense budgets can swing with Tuesday's midterms, and RBC and Bernstein cut targets to ~$360 last month on shipyard costs.
finance.target_note: Yahoo Finance analyst mean target (21 analysts), Nov 2

right: Gulfstream deliveries and shipyard hours keep climbing, as the CEO said on Friday's call
The raised 2026 outlook ($17.20 to $17.30 a share) holds or gets beaten
GD beats the S&P 500 from $372.59 by early February (that's the actual grade)
wrong: Midterm results put the defense budget on the chopping block
Submarine or Gulfstream supply-chain snags come back
The AI trade rips higher and leaves boring winners behind
catalyst.max: Everybody's panicking about AI capex. I'm buying a company that builds submarines and private jets. One of these is a lot harder to vibe-code.

ai.headline: OpenAI signs a batch of Abu Dhabi deals (ADNOC and G42 deploying its frontier models, Mubadala investment analysis, machine-readable government rules) as it courts UAE money for its $20 billion round
ai.why: When the U.S. checkbooks get lighter, you fly to Abu Dhabi. The Gulf is now a co-pilot on who funds frontier AI.

ai.headline: Aramco closes its deal for 49% of Saudi AI company HUMAIN, putting in about $2.6 billion in cash plus AI and compute assets; PIF keeps 51% and HUMAIN targets 3 gigawatts of data centers by 2030
ai.why: The world's biggest oil company is turning barrels into GPUs. Cheap power is the AI moat nobody can code around.

ai.headline: Blackstone tells investors Anthropic may get a high-yield 'junk' credit rating, likely double-B, after its IPO instead of investment grade
ai.why: A hot IPO and a junk rating can live in the same house. Debt-funded AI buildouts just got a little pricier to finance.

ai.headline: Grok API text gets an invisible watermark by default from Nov 7 across seven models, with an x-watermark header and opt-outs only for admins who confirm a legal exception
ai.why: Watermarks are going from research papers to default settings. If you ship AI text, assume it's tagged.

ai.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-Rosalind-6, a biology and drug-discovery reasoning model built on its GPT-6 flagship, available only to vetted labs through trusted access
ai.why: The most powerful biology AI ships with a bouncer at the door. Expect more 'too useful to release openly' models.

no_bets_note: Nothing cleared our bar at 7:10 AM ET across 20 NBA, NHL and NFL games with DraftKings lines, including Bears at Seahawks on Monday Night Football. Closest misses: Nets 11.5¢ at the Knicks (+2.2 pts, the biggest raw edge, but a long shot), Kings 21.5¢ at Dallas (+1.9, a long shot), Hornets 37.5¢ vs Detroit (+1.6, the best edge inside our 35-75¢ lean band, but under the 2.5 bar and the 40¢ pick floor), Wizards 44.5¢ at Orlando (+1.2, but DraftKings has moved away from them since the open), Cavaliers 60.5¢ vs OKC (+1.1). The Bears are 38.5¢ in Seattle, +0.6 vs a line that moved from +180 to +145. DraftKings lines via ESPN.

lean.label: Hornets
lean.market: NBA: DET @ CHA, Mon Nov 2 7:30 PM ET
lean.why: Not a bet, a lean. DraftKings has Charlotte at +145 at home, a 39.1% shot without the vig, and Polymarket sells it for 37.5¢: +1.6 points, short of our 2.5 bar and under the 40¢ floor. The one thing we like: the book has moved toward the Hornets since the open (+150 to +145), and Detroit is without Jalen Duren. The 5-1 Pistons are the better team. That's why it's a lean and not a proposal.
